title: Balloon Research
text: Along the way, I dug at various spots while Ren sniffed out all sorts of tools. Itsuki was busy scaling walls, too.
“It’s really starting to take shape,” Father said.
Click—Father snapped the pieces of a coelacanth model together like a puzzle, and there it was.
“That looks blatantly like something meant to be used for a specific purpose, doesn’t it?”
“Yeah. I’m sure we’ll end up using it somewhere.”
“And, well… the monsters showing up have changed a lot too.”
“No corpses popping out, at least. But yeah, that’s true.”
On the floor we were currently on, all sorts of Balloons appeared. When defeated, they turned to smoke and got sucked into our weapons as drops.
“Except for the monsters native to Cal Mira Island, everything turns to smoke… I wonder if that means something?”
“Maybe they’re not the real thing? Like, they’re just illusions reproduced by this dungeon or something.”
“That sounds about right.”
By the way, the bosses on this floor were Evil Balloon, Wing Balloon, and Metal Balloon.
“There sure are a lot of different kinds of Balloons.”
“They’re good monsters to hunt when you’ve just started a game, so there tend to be plenty of variety.”
“Indeed… ah, brings back memories, I say.”
“You’ve got memories of this too, Motoyasu?”

“Of course I do. Back when foolish young me used my authority to force a cowardly, underhanded duel upon Father, wagering Big Sister as the prize, Father threw a Balloon he’d hidden under his cloak and dealt me damage with it.”
Looking back now, it was a brilliant move, I say. Since Father takes no damage himself, he always kept one hidden under his cloak, ready to pull out and use as a weapon in a pinch.
“That’s a move born purely out of having no other means of attack. He really thought it through, didn’t he.”
“It’s an attack method none of us would ever think of. Though in Naofumi’s case, I guess Monster Player Killing is the more standard counterattack.”
“He probably could pull that off. Just think about all the monsters that gather around Naofumi-san when he’s taking a nap in a meadow somewhere…”
“Since we’re on the subject, mind actually shooing them away instead of just watching next time? Even if I don’t get hurt, you know.”
“I always figured that was some kind of Shield Hero special skill.”
“What about Ren, the Sword Hero? How does that work for him?”
Father seemed to be trying to rope Ren into the conversation.
“Didn’t the Sword Hero’s legends include something about reconciling with a dragon?”
“Hmph, nothing compared to the Shield Hero.”
Ren answered as though the notion were absurd, but Father, refusing to lose, raised a provocative hand toward him and said,
“With Luna-chan as an example, you can’t exactly deny it, Ren.”
“Gah… Motoyasu, what happened to the Balloon talk?”
Ren forcibly redirected the topic toward me.
“Ah yes, the tale of Balloons and Egg-gs being sent to swarm and attack me. I do wonder what would’ve happened if nothing had interrupted that duel with Father.”

I might well have managed to reclaim Big Sister, I say—if only that foolish Crimson Swine hadn’t launched such a witless attack. Truly, I was nothing but a clown back then. And yet… unable to move, subjected relentlessly to attacks on my vital points—Father’s own attacks didn’t hurt, but those Balloons certainly did. Surrender… no, the me of that time would never have surrendered. Yet it would’ve settled into a stalemate, the maximum resistance Father could muster. Eventually, I would have gradually defeated the Balloons one by one until Father ran out of his hand… and given that Father values the process as much as the outcome, I imagine he’d have looked at my battered face and groin, felt satisfied, and conceded defeat. Even so, Big Sister would likely have chosen to stay by Father’s side regardless.
“He’d probably be satisfied just from tormenting Motoyasu-kun, and even if Raphtalia-chan got confiscated from him, deep down he’d be frustrated—but he’d probably compromise to some extent anyway.”

No doubt about it—Father would convince himself he’d landed one good hit and let it go at that. Even if Big Sister still chose to follow him regardless. Different loop or not, Father is Father, I say. I feel like I understand him rather well.
“And after that, he probably started raising Balloons as a subweapon or something.”
“Quite possible. Filo-san probably would’ve bought some too, out of sheer desire for more firepower.”
“What happens if you actually raise a Balloon? Does it turn into a King Balloon or something?”
“My game knowledge doesn’t go that far, honestly…”
“Didn’t Rat say something about it? Something about there being a Legendary Balloon too?”
Doctor specializes in monsters, after all. She’d likely know about legends in that vein.

“She did give something like a lecture on it. I recall hearing about it during a class at the magic academy too. Apparently Balloons split off from a flying swarm-monster called the Balloon Legion and descend to the ground. And there’s supposedly some being spoken of as the pinnacle existence among them.”
“Raise one properly and it apparently becomes an Ad Balloon, about the size of a balance ball…”
Now that I think of it, I recall seeing from a distance an Ad Balloon tied to Father’s carriage for a while.
“Apparently there are Balloons on the verge of extinction too. Called Snake Balloon. Something about them being overhunted during some fad at the time.”
“I can kind of picture what shape that’d be. Probably snake-like, huh.”
“Like the balloons used in balloon-twisting tricks?”
“Probably? Balloon art, maybe? There’s something kind of romantic about that, isn’t there.”
“I remember shaping one into a sword and having a sword fight with it as a kid.”
Ah, the stick-shaped balloons. Those truly were the kind that thrilled a child’s heart, I say.

“Besides that, there’s probably other uses for them too, right? Like… given the shape, maybe the tail end gets used for something. Thin enough, just the right size, that sort of thing? Seems like it’d be a disaster if it tore, but if you can hunt one and get it that way, it’d be a lot easier than making one from scratch.”
“Itsuki, maybe you should keep your mouth shut on that one? Or are you deliberately aiming for that reaction?”
“Huh? What are you talking about?”
Ren tilted his head, unable to make the connection. Father flashed the smile only I could recognize as the one he wears right before telling a lie, and said to Ren,
“Water balloons. Just the right size for those, right?”
“Ah, I see.”
Itsuki looked like he had plenty more to say, but kept quiet.
“Raising Balloons, huh… I can picture leading one around on a leash like a dog for a walk. Pretty surreal image.”
“Ad Balloons really float up quite a bit, don’t they.”
“It’d be dreamy if you just turned one into an experimental hot-air balloon and rode it. Without Gaelion-chan or Fleon-chan around, you could probably still travel the skies.”
“You’d need some way to land, though.”
“Itsuki’s got reverse thrust, and Motoyasu’s basically got a propeller built in, so neither of you should have trouble.”
Emergency landings from the sky are indeed something one considers when riding an airplane. With enough effort, it would surely be possible, I say.
“Apparently among the Legendary Balloons there’s also a King Balloon, but there’s supposedly a monster called Hindenballoon in the legends too.”
“That sounds like a monster that’s gonna explode mid-air. Balloon evolutionary research sure runs deep, huh…”
“Filolial-sama runs deeper still, I say!”

More than Balloons, Filolial-sama comes first, Father! Filolial breeders were researching Filolial-sama’s speed for generations, and Yuki-chan is like the crystallized culmination of all that work, I say.

“I get it, I get it. I just meant it kind of makes sense why Rat-san’s so captivated. In the game you all played, were Balloons like this world’s equivalent of mascot monsters? Or was that the Filolials?”
Father asked, seeming genuinely curious about it.
“They weren’t treated as mascot monsters. If anything, that role belonged to the Usapiru.”
“Usapiru for Itsuki’s case, huh.”
“What about you, Ren-san?”
“Pikyu Pikyu, for me. Motoyasu, was it Filolial for you?”
I couldn’t bring myself to simply nod at Ren’s question. I could’ve easily lied, but that wouldn’t have been an honest answer to give Father.
“It’s quite difficult to answer, but no, it was not Filolial-sama.”
Now I could answer with Filolial-sama without hesitation, but back then, it wasn’t so, I say.
“Same as Itsuki—Usapiru filled the mascot slot for me.”
